metadata.author: Greg Paskal
metadata.description: X-Frame-Options header missing finding template with comprehensive guidance for all audiences including framework-specific implementation code, server configurations, and testing strategies to prevent clickjacking attacks where attackers embed the application in malicious iframes to trick users into performing unintended actions.

EXECUTIVE.summary: Your application lacks X-Frame-Options protection, leaving it vulnerable to clickjacking attacks where attackers trick users into clicking hidden buttons or links, potentially causing unauthorized transactions, data theft, or account compromise.
EXECUTIVE.businessRisk: Moderate risk of clickjacking attacks leading to unauthorized transactions, fraudulent fund transfers, password changes, or account takeovers. Attackers embed your site in invisible iframes on malicious pages to deceive users. Can damage customer trust and brand reputation. Financial services and banking applications face elevated risk. Average remediation cost for clickjacking exploits ranges from $50K-$200K including customer reimbursement and reputation repair.
EXECUTIVE.complianceImpact: OWASP Top 10 A04:2021 (Insecure Design) category. PCI-DSS Requirement 6.5.9 addresses clickjacking prevention. NIST 800-63B authentication guidelines recommend frame-busting protections. May trigger security audit findings requiring remediation for compliance certification.

PROJECT_MANAGER.summary: Missing X-Frame-Options header allows attackers to embed application in malicious iframes, enabling clickjacking attacks that trick users into unintended actions. Quick fix: add HTTP response header.
PROJECT_MANAGER.timeline: Should be addressed within 1-2 sprints. Implementation takes 1-2 hours including testing. Low complexity change with minimal risk. Priority increases to HIGH for financial applications, admin panels, or any system with sensitive transactions.
PROJECT_MANAGER.effort: 1-2 hours for implementation and testing. Low-risk change with minimal code modification.
dependencies: Access to web server or application configuration
QA testing resources for iframe embedding tests

DEVELOPER.summary: X-Frame-Options HTTP response header is not present, allowing application to be embedded in iframes on any domain, creating clickjacking vulnerability.
DEVELOPER.technical: X-Frame-Options is a legacy HTTP response header (pre-CSP) that controls whether a browser should allow a page to be rendered within a frame, iframe, embed, or object tag. Without this header, attackers can embed your application in invisible iframes and overlay malicious content to trick users into clicking hidden elements (clickjacking/UI redressing). Three values exist: DENY (no framing allowed), SAMEORIGIN (only same-origin framing), ALLOW-FROM uri (deprecated, use CSP frame-ancestors instead). Modern approach: use both X-Frame-Options and CSP frame-ancestors directive for defense-in-depth. X-Frame-Options supported by all modern browsers (IE8+, Chrome 4+, Firefox 3.6+, Safari 4+).
DEVELOPER.vulnerability: CWE-1021 (Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames). Clickjacking attacks overlay transparent iframes to capture clicks intended for visible content. Attack scenarios: (1) Invisible iframe overlay tricks user into transferring funds, (2) Hidden 'Like' button click for social engineering, (3) Webcam/microphone permission theft, (4) OAuth token theft through click manipulation, (5) Administrative action execution (delete account, change password). Combined with social engineering, highly effective against non-technical users.

SECURITY_ENGINEER.summary: Missing X-Frame-Options header enables clickjacking attacks through iframe embedding, allowing UI redressing attacks that manipulate user interactions for malicious purposes.
SECURITY_ENGINEER.vulnerability: CWE-1021 (Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers), CWE-451 (User Interface Misrepresentation). Clickjacking exploits user interface confusion by overlaying transparent iframes. Without X-Frame-Options, application can be embedded anywhere, enabling: cursor hijacking, drag-and-drop hijacking, keystroke logging through overlay, likejacking (social media), cookie theft through cross-frame scripting when combined with other vulnerabilities.
SECURITY_ENGINEER.attackVector: Attacker creates malicious webpage embedding victim site in invisible iframe. User visits attacker site thinking they're clicking visible content, but actually interacting with hidden iframe. Attack chain: (1) Embed target site in transparent iframe, (2) Position iframe under cursor, (3) Overlay fake UI with enticing content, (4) User clicks fake button, actually clicks real button in hidden iframe, (5) Execute unauthorized action (transfer funds, grant permissions, etc.). Requires no technical sophistication - point-and-click attack tools publicly available.
SECURITY_ENGINEER.threatLevel: MEDIUM - Less prevalent than XSS/CSRF but significant impact when exploited. Particularly dangerous for: banking/financial applications, admin panels, OAuth authorization flows, social media platforms, e-commerce checkout. Modern defense-in-depth includes both X-Frame-Options and CSP frame-ancestors. Browser support universal across all modern browsers.
SECURITY_ENGINEER.mitigationUrgency: Implement within 2-4 weeks. Higher priority (1-2 weeks) for financial applications or admin interfaces. Low implementation complexity with minimal risk. Deploy alongside CSP frame-ancestors directive for comprehensive protection. Test thoroughly to ensure legitimate iframe usage (if any) still functions.

OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.summary: Web servers not configured to send X-Frame-Options header, requiring HTTP response header configuration across all web server infrastructure.
OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.technical: X-Frame-Options header must be added to HTTP responses at web server, reverse proxy, or application layer. Header syntax: X-Frame-Options: DENY (block all framing) or X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN (allow same-origin framing only). ALLOW-FROM deprecated - use CSP frame-ancestors instead. Typically configured in Nginx, Apache, load balancers, or application middleware. Modern best practice: use both X-Frame-Options (legacy browser support) and CSP frame-ancestors directive.
OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.scope: All web servers serving application traffic: production web servers, load balancers, CDN origin shields, API gateways (if serving HTML), reverse proxies. Must be consistent across all environments (dev, staging, production). Consider impact on legitimate iframe usage: embedded widgets, SSO flows, iframe-based integrations.
OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.monitoring: Monitor for legitimate iframe usage that might break after implementing X-Frame-Options. Check error logs for frame-related errors. Use browser DevTools to verify header present. Test from external sites attempting to embed application. Monitor for clickjacking attack attempts in security logs (difficult to detect). Use security scanners to continuously verify header configuration.

QA_TESTER.summary: Missing X-Frame-Options header prevents validation that application properly blocks malicious iframe embedding and clickjacking attack vectors.
QA_TESTER.testImplication: Cannot validate clickjacking prevention controls. Security testing tools (Burp Suite, OWASP ZAP) flag missing X-Frame-Options as medium-severity finding. After implementation, must test: (1) Application cannot be embedded in external iframes (DENY), (2) Application can be embedded in same-origin iframes if using SAMEORIGIN, (3) Legitimate iframe usage still works if required, (4) Browser console shows frame-blocking errors when appropriate.
QA_TESTER.riskIfNotFixed: Security audit failure. Penetration test findings. PCI-DSS compliance gaps. Actual clickjacking exploitation in production leading to unauthorized transactions, account compromises, or data theft. Financial applications face elevated risk of fraud. Reputation damage from successful attacks.

generic.code:
# Generic X-Frame-Options Implementation Guidelines

## Header Syntax

X-Frame-Options: DENY
  - Blocks all framing (recommended for most applications)
  - Use when application should never be embedded

X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN
  - Allows framing only by same-origin pages
  - Use when application needs to embed itself

X-Frame-Options: ALLOW-FROM https://example.com
  - DEPRECATED - Do not use
  - Poor browser support
  - Use CSP frame-ancestors instead

## Modern Approach: CSP frame-ancestors

# Equivalent to X-Frame-Options: DENY
Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'

# Equivalent to X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN
Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self'

# Allow specific origins (modern alternative to ALLOW-FROM)
Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors https://trusted.com https://other-trusted.com

## Best Practice: Defense-in-Depth

# Set both headers for maximum compatibility
X-Frame-Options: DENY
Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'

## Implementation Decision Tree

1. Does your app ever need to be embedded in iframes?
   NO  → Use DENY + frame-ancestors 'none'
   YES → Continue to step 2

2. Only embed in your own pages (same origin)?
   YES → Use SAMEORIGIN + frame-ancestors 'self'
   NO  → Continue to step 3

3. Need to allow specific external domains?
   YES → Use CSP frame-ancestors with whitelist
        Do NOT use X-Frame-Options ALLOW-FROM (deprecated)

## Common Use Cases

### Banking/Financial Applications
X-Frame-Options: DENY
Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'

### Admin Panels
X-Frame-Options: DENY
Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'

### E-commerce Checkout
X-Frame-Options: DENY
Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'

### Embeddable Widgets
Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors *
(No X-Frame-Options header)

### OAuth/SSO Flows
X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN
Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self'

### Documentation Sites
X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN
Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self'

# Generic X-Frame-Options Testing ## Browser DevTools Testing 1. Open browser DevTools (F12) 2. Go to Network tab 3. Navigate to your site 4. Click on the HTML document request 5. Go to Headers section 6. Look for X-Frame-Options in Response Headers ## Command-Line Testing # Check if X-Frame-Options header is present curl -I https://your-domain.com | grep -i x-frame-options # Expected output: X-Frame-Options: DENY # View all response headers curl -I https://your-domain.com # Test multiple pages for path in / /login /dashboard /api/data; do echo "Testing $path:" curl -I https://your-domain.com$path | grep -i x-frame-options done ## Manual Iframe Embedding Test 1. Create test HTML file (test-iframe.html): Iframe Test

Attempting to embed site in iframe:

If X-Frame-Options is working, the iframe will be blocked

2. Open test-iframe.html in browser 3. Check browser console for errors like: "Refused to display 'https://your-domain.com' in a frame because it set 'X-Frame-Options' to 'deny'." ## Online Testing Tools 1. Security Headers Scanner https://securityheaders.com/ - Enter your domain - Check for X-Frame-Options header 2. Mozilla Observatory https://observatory.mozilla.org/ - Comprehensive security scan - Checks X-Frame-Options and CSP 3. SSL Labs https://www.ssllabs.com/ssltest/ - Includes HTTP header analysis ## Automated Testing Script #!/bin/bash # test-xfo.sh URL="$1" if [ -z "$URL" ]; then echo "Usage: $0 " exit 1 fi echo "Testing X-Frame-Options for: $URL" # Test X-Frame-Options header XFO=$(curl -s -I "$URL" | grep -i "^x-frame-options:" | cut -d: -f2 | tr -d '\r\n ') if [ -z "$XFO" ]; then echo "❌ X-Frame-Options header is MISSING" exit 1 else echo "✅ X-Frame-Options: $XFO" if [ "$XFO" == "DENY" ]; then echo "✅ Using DENY (most secure)" elif [ "$XFO" == "SAMEORIGIN" ]; then echo "âš ï¸ Using SAMEORIGIN (ensure this is intended)" elif [[ "$XFO" == ALLOW-FROM* ]]; then echo "❌ Using deprecated ALLOW-FROM directive" fi fi # Check for CSP frame-ancestors CSP=$(curl -s -I "$URL" | grep -i "^content-security-policy:") if echo "$CSP" | grep -q "frame-ancestors"; then echo "✅ CSP frame-ancestors directive present (defense-in-depth)" else echo "âš ï¸ CSP frame-ancestors not found (consider adding)" fi

verificationSteps: Deploy to staging environment first
Verify X-Frame-Options header present using: curl -I https://your-domain.com | grep X-Frame-Options
Test in browser DevTools: Network tab > Headers > Response Headers
Create test HTML with iframe embedding your site - should be blocked
Check browser console for frame-blocking error message
Test all critical pages have the header (homepage, login, dashboard, checkout)
If using SAMEORIGIN, verify same-origin embedding still works
Test any legitimate iframe usage hasn't broken (widgets, SSO, etc.)
Run security scanner (securityheaders.com) to verify header configuration
Test across multiple browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge)
Verify both X-Frame-Options and CSP frame-ancestors present
Monitor application logs for any frame-related errors after deployment

apache.config:
# Apache - Add X-Frame-Options header
# /etc/apache2/sites-available/your-site.conf or .htaccess

<VirtualHost *:443>
    ServerName your-domain.com
    
    # Enable mod_headers if not already enabled
    # a2enmod headers
    
    # Add X-Frame-Options header
    Header always set X-Frame-Options "DENY"
    # Or for same-origin framing:
    # Header always set X-Frame-Options "SAMEORIGIN"
    
    # Also add CSP frame-ancestors for defense-in-depth
    Header always set Content-Security-Policy "frame-ancestors 'none'"
    # Or: Header always set Content-Security-Policy "frame-ancestors 'self'"
    
    # Other recommended security headers
    Header always set X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff"
    Header always set X-XSS-Protection "1; mode=block"
    Header always set Referrer-Policy "strict-origin-when-cross-origin"
    Header always set Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains"
    
    DocumentRoot /var/www/html
    
    <Directory /var/www/html>
        Options -Indexes +FollowSymLinks
        AllowOverride All
        Require all granted
    </Directory>
    
    SSLEngine on
    SSLCertificateFile /etc/ssl/certs/your-cert.crt
    SSLCertificateKeyFile /etc/ssl/private/your-key.key
</VirtualHost>

# Alternative: .htaccess file
<IfModule mod_headers.c>
  Header always set X-Frame-Options "DENY"
  Header always set Content-Security-Policy "frame-ancestors 'none'"
</IfModule>
apache.reload:
# Enable headers module if not enabled
sudo a2enmod headers

# Test Apache configuration

aws-cloudfront.config:
# AWS CloudFront - Add X-Frame-Options via Response Headers Policy

# AWS CLI - Create Response Headers Policy
aws cloudfront create-response-headers-policy \
  --response-headers-policy-config '{
    "Name": "SecurityHeadersPolicy",
    "Comment": "Security headers including X-Frame-Options",
    "SecurityHeadersConfig": {
      "XFrameOptions": {
        "FrameOption": "DENY",
        "Override": true
      },
      "ContentSecurityPolicy": {
        "ContentSecurityPolicy": "frame-ancestors '\''none'\'';",
        "Override": true
      },
      "StrictTransportSecurity": {
        "AccessControlMaxAgeSec": 31536000,
        "IncludeSubdomains": true,
        "Override": true
      }
    }
  }'

# CloudFormation Template
Resources:
  ResponseHeadersPolicy:
    Type: AWS::CloudFront::ResponseHeadersPolicy
    Properties:
      ResponseHeadersPolicyConfig:
        Name: SecurityHeadersPolicy
        Comment: Security headers including X-Frame-Options
        SecurityHeadersConfig:
          XFrameOptions:
            FrameOption: DENY  # or SAMEORIGIN
            Override: true
          ContentSecurityPolicy:
            ContentSecurityPolicy: "frame-ancestors 'none';"
            Override: true
          StrictTransportSecurity:
            AccessControlMaxAgeSec: 31536000
            IncludeSubdomains: true
            Override: true
          XContentTypeOptions:
            Override: true
          ReferrerPolicy:
            ReferrerPolicy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin
            Override: true

  CloudFrontDistribution:
    Type: AWS::CloudFront::Distribution
    Properties:
      DistributionConfig:
        Origins:
          - DomainName: your-origin.example.com
            Id: MyOrigin
            CustomOriginConfig:
              HTTPPort: 80
              HTTPSPort: 443
              OriginProtocolPolicy: https-only
        DefaultCacheBehavior:
          TargetOriginId: MyOrigin
          ViewerProtocolPolicy: redirect-to-https
          ResponseHeadersPolicyId: !Ref ResponseHeadersPolicy
        Enabled: true

# Terraform Example
resource "aws_cloudfront_response_headers_policy" "security_headers" {
  name    = "security-headers-policy"
  comment = "Security headers including X-Frame-Options"

  security_headers_config {
    frame_options {
      frame_option = "DENY"  # or "SAMEORIGIN"
      override     = true
    }

    content_security_policy {
      content_security_policy = "frame-ancestors 'none';"
      override                = true
    }

    strict_transport_security {
      access_control_max_age_sec = 31536000
      include_subdomains         = true
      override                   = true
    }
  }
}

resource "aws_cloudfront_distribution" "main" {
  # ... other configuration ...

  default_cache_behavior {
    # ... other settings ...
    response_headers_policy_id = aws_cloudfront_response_headers_policy.security_headers.id
  }
}
aws-cloudfront.reload:
# No reload needed - CloudFront changes propagate automatically

# Check deployment status
aws cloudfront get-distribution \
  --id DISTRIBUTION_ID \
  --query 'Distribution.Status'

# Wait for deployment to complete (can take 5-15 minutes)
aws cloudfront wait distribution-deployed \
  --id DISTRIBUTION_ID

# List all distributions
aws cloudfront list-distributions \
  --query "DistributionList.Items[].{ID:Id,Status:Status,Domain:DomainName}"

# Get response headers policy details
aws cloudfront get-response-headers-policy \
  --id POLICY_ID
aws-cloudfront.verify:
# Test X-Frame-Options header from CloudFront
curl -I https://your-cloudfront-domain.cloudfront.net | grep -i x-frame-options

# Test from your custom domain
curl -I https://your-domain.com | grep -i x-frame-options

# View all response headers
curl -I https://your-domain.com

# Test multiple edge locations
for region in us-east-1 us-west-2 eu-west-1 ap-southeast-1; do
  echo "Testing from $region:"
  curl -I https://your-domain.com | grep -i x-frame
  sleep 2
done

# Verify cache behavior doesn't strip headers
curl -I https://your-domain.com -H "Cache-Control: no-cache"

OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.rollbackPlan:
1. Keep backup of current server configuration files
2. Document current header configuration
3. If X-Frame-Options breaks legitimate iframe usage, temporarily remove header
4. For Nginx: Comment out header line, test with 'nginx -t', reload with 'nginx -s reload'
5. For Apache: Comment out header line, test with 'apachectl configtest', reload with 'systemctl reload apache2'
6. For AWS CloudFront: Modify Response Headers Policy to remove X-Frame-Options, wait for propagation
7. Identify which iframe usage broke (widgets, SSO, integrations)
8. Either: (a) Use SAMEORIGIN if same-origin framing, or (b) Use CSP frame-ancestors with specific whitelist
9. Re-deploy with adjusted policy
10. Test thoroughly before production deployment
verificationSteps: 1. Verify header present: curl -I https://your-domain.com | grep -i x-frame-options
2. Create test HTML file with iframe embedding your site
3. Open test HTML in browser - iframe should be blocked
4. Check browser console for error: 'Refused to display ... because it set X-Frame-Options'
5. Test all application pages have header (homepage, login, API endpoints)
6. If using SAMEORIGIN, verify same-origin embedding works
7. Test legitimate iframe usage hasn't broken (SSO, widgets, integrations)
8. Run securityheaders.com scan - should pass X-Frame-Options check
9. Verify both X-Frame-Options and CSP frame-ancestors present
10. Test across multiple browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge)
11. Check CDN/load balancer propagation complete (5-15 minutes for CloudFront)
12. Monitor application logs for iframe-related errors

manualTests.name: Verify X-Frame-Options Header Present
steps: 5. Click on the first request (HTML document)
manualTests.expected: X-Frame-Options header present with value 'DENY' (recommended) or 'SAMEORIGIN'. CSP frame-ancestors directive also present for defense-in-depth.

manualTests.name: Test Iframe Embedding Blocked
steps: 2. Add iframe embedding your site: <iframe src='https://your-domain.com' width='800' height='600'></iframe>
5. Observe iframe area - should be blank/blocked
7. Expected error: 'Refused to display ... because it set X-Frame-Options to DENY'
9. Verify all pages blocked in iframe
manualTests.expected: If X-Frame-Options is DENY: All pages blocked in iframe with console error. If SAMEORIGIN: External iframe blocked, same-origin iframe allowed.

manualTests.name: Test Same-Origin Embedding (if using SAMEORIGIN)
steps: 1. Only perform this test if X-Frame-Options is set to SAMEORIGIN
2. Create test page on same domain
3. Add iframe embedding another page from same domain
8. Create test page on different domain (or use jsfiddle.net)
9. Attempt to embed site - should be blocked
manualTests.expected: Same-origin embedding works. Cross-origin embedding blocked with console error.

manualTests.name: Verify Legitimate Iframe Usage Still Works
steps: 1. Identify any legitimate iframe usage in application
2. Examples: embedded widgets, SSO login flows, payment gateways
4. For widgets: Verify they load and function correctly
5. For SSO: Complete authentication flow, verify success
6. For payments: Test checkout process end-to-end
7. Check browser console for any frame-related errors
8. If anything breaks, document specific scenario
10. May need to use SAMEORIGIN or CSP whitelist
manualTests.expected: All legitimate iframe usage continues to function correctly. No unexpected errors or broken features. If issues found, policy needs adjustment (SAMEORIGIN or CSP frame-ancestors whitelist).

verificationSteps: 1. Clear all browser cache and cookies
2. Open browser DevTools (F12) and go to Network tab
3. Navigate to application homepage
4. Verify X-Frame-Options header in response headers
5. Create test HTML with iframe embedding site - should fail
6. Check browser console for 'Refused to display' error
7. Test all critical pages (login, checkout, dashboard) have header
8. Test legitimate iframe usage still works (if applicable)

10. Run automated Selenium/Playwright tests - all should pass
11. Run securityheaders.com scan - X-Frame-Options should pass
